elements.element: Renewal requires mutual written agreement unless every conditional automatic-renewal element below is met.
elements.evidence: Rendered Article IV(I) now reads "The Agreement may be renewed only by mutual written agreement of the parties," replacing Licensor's unilateral seven-year extension option; this is consistent with retained IV(II) ("extended by mutual written of the parties") and IV(III) ("by mutual agreement in writing").

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, each renewal term is no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: after the edit there is no automatic renewal mechanic anywhere in Article IV — renewal occurs only on affirmative mutual written agreement, so no renewal-term length needs to be fixed.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer may opt out on no more than 30 days' notice.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal is not automatic, so Licensee is never rolled into a further term and needs no opt-out notice window; the term simply expires at the close of the 36-month Initial Period absent mutual written agreement.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Vendor must remind Customer at least 60 days before renewal.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no automatic renewal survives the edit, so no Licensor reminder mechanic is required to protect Licensee from an unnoticed rollover.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at the lesser of CPI and 3 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: renewal only occurs by mutual written agreement (so any pricing would be agreed at that time) and the cited fee provisions contain no renewal price-escalation or uplift mechanic to cap.

elements.element: If renewal is automatic, Customer's non-renewal notice window is no more than 60 days.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: the rendered clause contains no automatic-renewal trigger, so no non-renewal notice window arises for Licensee.

elements.element: If renewal permits price increases, each increase is capped at 5 percent.
elements.evidence: Condition does not apply: no renewal price-increase mechanic exists in the rendered clause or the fee article; pricing on any mutually agreed extension is negotiated, not unilaterally escalated.

reasons: The original sentence gave Licensor a unilateral option to extend for seven (7) years — an automatic/unilateral multi-year renewal with no Licensee notice window at all, which is walk-away territory and fails the fallback; the finding status 'deviation' is correct.

The edit is confined to the single offending sentence: only "for an additional period of seven (7) years at the option of the Licensor" was replaced with "only by mutual written agreement of the parties." Termination-for-breach language, Licensor's retained payment rights, and Articles IV(II) and IV(III) are left untouched, so nothing outside the checklist was altered or deleted.

No extras were added — no reminder mechanic, uplift cap, survival tail, or procedure was inserted, because the mutual-agreement limb of the preferred position makes each conditional element inapplicable.

Intent is preserved and internal consistency improves: the amended IV(I) now aligns with IV(II)'s 45-day mutual-extension mechanic and IV(III)'s mutual-written-extension requirement rather than contradicting them; no defined term, cross-reference, or commercial mechanic is left dangling.

Both levels are position-complete, so the redline can be presented at the preferred position with the margin comment's automatic-renewal fallback (12-month terms, ≤60-day window, ≤5% uplift) held in reserve.
